blocks.text: B1-17 · Reading without vowels: disambiguation
Lesson overview

From the module B1.3 Readings are without vowels, such as newspapers, websites and messages. An Arabic reader does not see the vowels, he reconstructs them: the same spelling ⁧علم⁩ may be ⁧عِلْم⁩ • science • ⁧عَلَم⁩ The flag of the country concerned shall be the flag of the Union. ⁧عَلِمَ⁩ • came to know, or ⁧عَلَّمَ⁩ The reader chooses in a fraction of a second thanks to grammar and context. In this unit make this choice aware: learn the five most frequent types of ambiguity (active or passive, verb or name, simple or derived form, verb person, prefix or root), the grammatical spies that resolve them and a strategy in five steps. You also start the timed reading: at the end of B1 you will have to read short news in silence at least 70 words per minute, with a summary. Three weeks.

rows: B1-15, B1-16; modules B1.1 and B1.2 (verbal, passive form, order of sentence)
18–20 hours · three weeks (weeks 130–132), plus the EGY track

blocks.text: Materials This unit, dictionary by root, a chronometer (also the phone), script for speech synthesis, sessions with the tutor
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. recognize the five main types of ambiguity of an unvocalised text;
2. use grammatical spies (article, prepositions, particles) to decide between name and verb;
3. to distinguish active and passive, form I and forms II and IV, persons of the verb, prefixes and radical letters;
4. apply a strategy in five steps to a new sentence;
5. read silently an unvocalized text of 150 words to 50–60 words per minute and summarize it in English.
Three-week plan.

2. As an Arab reads
A text that is not spoken is not a text that is difficult: it is a text that asks the reader to participate. Three facts to know.
1. Consonants and long vowels are almost always enough. In a normal sentence only one in five words or
six really has as many readings as possible; for the others there is only one that makes sense.
2. Grammar works for you. The position in the sentence, article, prepositions, particles and agreement
delete most of the readings.
3. Case terminations can be left aside. To understand enough the internal vowel ( ⁧كَتَبَ⁩ or ⁧كُتِبَ⁩ ? ⁧دَرَسَ⁩ or

⁧دَرَّسَ⁩ ?); desinences are useful when you read aloud in a formal way. The five most frequent ambiguities are: active or passive (section 3), verb or name (section 4), simple or derived form (section 5), person of the verb (section 7), prefix or root (section 8).
3. Active or passive?
Internal liabilities (B1-05) changes only vowels: without vowels ⁧أعلن⁩ may be ⁧أَعْلَنَ⁩ • announced • ⁧أُعْلِنَ⁩ It was announced.

rows: There is one who acts (the ministry) and there is one object: active
a meeting does not hold anything: passive

blocks.text: ⁧نُقِلَ المُصَابُونَ إِلَى المُسْتَشْفَىنقل المصابون إلى المستشفى⁩ the injured are transported: passive

The passive spies. After the verb there is only one thing or person who suffers, and no complement object; the subject is something that cannot act ( ⁧اِجْتِمَاع⁩ , ⁧نَتَائِج⁩ , ⁧قَرَار⁩ ). Some verbs of the chronicle are almost always passive: ⁧أُصِيبَ⁩ He was wounded. ⁧تُوُفِّيَ⁩ "He died" ⁧عُيِّنَ⁩ “was appointed”. Construction ⁧تَمَّ⁩ + maṣdar ( ⁧تَمَّ إِعْلَانُ النَّتَائِجِ⁩ ) is never ambiguous: that's why newspapers use it so much.
4. Word or name?
Many frequent roots have name and verb with the same consonants.

rows: ⁧عِلْمعلم⁩ ʿilm Science · ⁧عَلَم⁩ ʿalam Flag of the European Union ⁧عَلِمَ⁩ ʿalima "He knew" · ⁧عَلَّمَ⁩ ʿallama "Teached"
ḥukm Judgment; Government ⁧حَكَم⁩ ḥakam .... ⁧حَكَمَ⁩ ḥakama He judged, ruled, ruled. ⁧حُكْمحكم⁩
⁧شِعْرشعر⁩ šiʿr "Poetry" · ⁧شَعْر⁩ šaʿr Hair ⁧شَعَرَ⁩ šaʿara He felt, tried, tried.

blocks.text: How do you decide? After the article or a preposition there is a name: ⁧فِي العِلْمِ⁩ , ⁧بِالعَمَلِ⁩ . A word followed by a name to the name that may be its subject at the beginning of the sentence is probably a verb: ⁧عَمِلَ أَبِي فِي مِصْرَ⁩ . A word that holds a genitive (iḍāfa) is a name: ⁧عَمَلُ أَبِي⁩ It's my father's work. And the meaning decides the last choice: ⁧عَلَمُ البَلَدِ⁩ The flag of the country is not the science of the country.
5. Simple form or derivative?
The šadda of the II form and hamza of the IV usually do not write.
⁧اعلن⁩ — ⁧أَعْلَنَ⁩ aʿlana "Annunciò" (IV) · ⁧أُعْلِنَ⁩ uʿlina It was announced.

How do you decide? Look at the regency: ⁧قَدِمَ⁩ holds ⁧مِنْ⁩ or ⁧إِلَى⁩ ( ⁧قَدِمَ مِنَ القَاهِرَةِ⁩ ), ⁧قَدَّمَ⁩ holds an object ( ⁧قَدَّمَ اسْتِقَالَتَهُ⁩ ). Look who's doing it: ⁧دَرَّسَ⁩ , the student is ⁧دَرَسَ⁩ . Look at the number of objects: two objects often indicate the II shape ( ⁧عَلَّمَهُ الحِسَابَ⁩ He taught him arithmetic. And remember that many newspapers omit the hamza on the alife: ⁧اعلن⁩ , ⁧احمد⁩ , ⁧ان⁩ are ⁧أَعْلَنَ⁩ , ⁧أَحْمَد⁩ , ⁧أَنْ⁩ or ⁧إِنَّ⁩ .

7. The person of the verb and the pronouns
The perfect in -t. No vowels ⁧كتبت⁩ has five readings:

rows: a vocation ⁧يَا⁩ ... a question to someone
a female subject after the verb: ⁧كَتَبَتْ هُدَى⁩
no staff member; the subject is one thing: ⁧كُتِبَتِ الرِّسَالَةُ⁩

blocks.text: The imperfect with ⁧ت⁩ . ⁧تكتب⁩ è ⁧تَكْتُبُ⁩ You write to her or she writes to her, or ⁧تُكْتَبُ⁩ It is written in the form of a letter. Search the subject:
⁧أَنْتَ تَكْتُبُ⁩ , ⁧هُدَى تَكْتُبُ⁩ , ⁧تُكْتَبُ التَّقَارِيرُ.⁩

The suffixes. ⁧كتابك⁩ è ⁧كِتَابُكَ⁩ or ⁧كِتَابُكِ⁩ : decides the person to whom we speak. ⁧كتبه⁩ may be ⁧كَتَبَهُ⁩ ......... ⁧كُتُبُهُ⁩ His books are in. The reference of the pronoun ( ⁧المَرْجِع⁩ ). A pronoun ⁧ـهُ⁩ or ⁧ـهَا⁩ usually refers to the nearest name of the same genre and number that makes sense. In ⁧وَصَلَ الوَزِيرُ إِلَى المَدِينَةِ وَزَارَ مُسْتَشْفَاهَا⁩ , ⁧ـهَا⁩ is the city (feminine), not the minister. With non-human plurals the pronoun is feminine singular: ⁧الكُتُبُ⁩ … ⁧قَرَأْتُهَا⁩ .
8. Prefix or root?
Particles ⁧و⁩ , ⁧فـ⁩ , ⁧بـ⁩ , ⁧لـ⁩ , ⁧كـ⁩ they stick to the word that follows. A word beginning with one of these letters may contain a particle or a letter of the root.

rows: ⁧وَلِي⁩ wa-lī I have a maximum content by weight of not more than 5% of the total weight of the product
⁧لِلطُّلَّابِ⁩ li-ṭ-ṭullāb For students ( ⁧لِـ⁩ + ⁧الـ⁩ : the alife falls)

blocks.text: How do you decide? First try reading with the root: if the word exists and the phrase works, that's it. Then look at what follows: ⁧فقد⁩ + a verb to the perfect is ⁧فَقَدْ⁩ ( ⁧فَقَدْ وَصَلَ⁩ In fact, he arrived. ⁧فقد⁩ + an object is ⁧فَقَدَ⁩ ( ⁧فَقَدَ جَوَازَ سَفَرِهِ⁩ He lost his passport. Warning to ⁧لل⁩ : it's always ⁧لِـ⁩ + Article.
9. The strategy in five steps
The grammar spies.

rows: a verb to the conjunctive imperfect

blocks.text: ⁧كَأَنَّ⁩ · ⁧لٰكِنَّ⁩ · ⁧أَنَّ⁩ · ⁧إِنَّ⁩ a name or pronoun to the accused
The five steps.
1. Read the whole sentence without stopping, even if you don't understand everything.
2. Find the main verb and subject (B1-08). If you don't find a verb, ask yourself what word it might
I'm not.
3. Use spies: article and prepositions announce a name; ⁧أَنْ⁩ , ⁧لَمْ⁩ , ⁧قَدْ⁩ They announce a verb.
4. Check accord and regency: gender and number of the subject, preposition of the verb ( ⁧عَلِمَ بِـ⁩ , ⁧قَدِمَ مِنْ⁩ ,
⁧حَكَمَ عَلَى⁩ ).
5. Choose the most natural reading in the kind of text: in the news the passive is frequent, in the titles the imperfect
often indicates a past fact (B1-15), in the news reports are back the placements of B1-16.
10. Pronunciation

Read aloud an unvocalized text. First you read in silence a sentence, then say it out loud: never read a word before you understand the phrase. Speak the internal vowels carefully (kutiba, darrasa); for case terminations you have two possibilities: to read them all, like a conductor, or to read Don't invent random terminations: better pause than a mistake. Hidden shaddas. When you choose the II form, make it feel: darrasa, qaddama, ʿallama, waqqaʿa. It's the difference your listener uses to understand.

Timed reading. Read the text in silence, only once, with the stopwatch. Don't go back and don't use the dictionary. Then close the book and write a summary of three sentences in English.
